name: Martine: Benchmarking Multi-View 3D Surface Reconstruction Across Viewpoint Coverage, Resolution, and Lighting
description: Martine is a high-precision benchmark for controlled multi-view 3D surface reconstruction. It comprises 28 real-world objects — including transparent, specular, low-texture, and fine-structured items — captured at 9568×6376 resolution from 84 viewpoints over a spherical cap (20°–70° elevation), under both single-light and multi-light (30-LED) acquisition regimes. Martine provides object-independent camera calibration with quantified accuracy (0.542 px reprojection error, about 0.04 mm), sub-millimetric ground-truth meshes for 26 objects (Artec Spider optical scanner and CT scanning) with measured image-to-geometry alignment residuals (1.22 px mean leave-one-out reprojection error, below 2 px for all 26 objects), and 3D property masks (Lambertian, specular, transparent, textureless, fine structure, high curvature, low visibility) enabling error analysis by object property. We benchmark representative methods from photogrammetry, classical multi-view stereo, Gaussian-splatting-based reconstruction, neural implicit surfaces, and multi-view photometric stereo; the best observed mean Chamfer distance is 0.058 mm over the evaluated visible surface. Download scripts, documentation of the file structure, and format converters are available at https://github.com/martine-benchmark/martine-dataset; project page: https://martine-benchmark.github.io/.
